vulnerability.category_l2: Unauthenticated PHP object deserialization of frames received on a TCP listener bound to all interfaces by default

critical_operation.description: ServerLogCommand::execute() starts a TCP listener and passes every received line to unserialize(base64_decode($message)) with no allowed_classes argument, no signature or integrity check, and no authentication. Because configure() defaults --host to 0.0.0.0:9911, any host that can reach the port can deliver a frame; the only rejection afterwards is false === $record, which does not prevent magic methods from running during deserialization. displayLog() then requires array $record, so a non-array payload raises a type error after the payload has been instantiated. The 5.4.52 fix defaults the host to 127.0.0.1:9911, restricts unserialize() to VarDumper Data/Stub classes and discards non-array records.

entry_point.description: A TCP connection to the server:log listener on port 9911. With the default --host 0.0.0.0:9911 the listener accepts connections on every interface, not only loopback.

trace.description: getLogs() accepts each incoming connection with stream_socket_accept() and yields every fgets() line as a message
execute() passes the base64-decoded frame to unserialize() without allowed_classes
displayLog() declares array $record, so a non-array payload fails after deserialization has already run

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read ServerLogCommand::execute at v5.4.45 and confirm unserialize(base64_decode($message)) has no allowed_classes and no prior authentication.
An independent reviewer must confirm the default --host is 0.0.0.0:9911 and that getLogs() accepts off-host connections.
An independent reviewer must confirm 0891b2f2 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.52, and that the fix changes the host default, adds the allowlist and the is_array gate.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.52.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PHP, socket listener, serialized payload or gadget chain was executed; the finding is static.
Exploitation beyond denial of service depends on usable gadget chains in the target autoload set, as the advisory itself notes.
The listener is a development-time helper; exposure depends on running server:log on a reachable host.
Only the 5.4 branch was fetched and compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
The OSV CVSS_V4 vector (AT:N/VC:H/VI:H) differs from the CNA vector and carries no separately published numeric score.

The symfony.com blog says the allowlist covers Symfony\Component\VarDumper\Caster\* and Cloner\* classes, while the code allows only Data and Stub (both in Cloner); the blog wording is broader than the implementation.
open_questions: Whether ServerLogHandler exposes a similar unsafe path on the producer side was not audited.
Whether the same default host appears in the 6.x/7.x/8.x branches was not checked.
